claims.statement: In one 45-year-old epilepsy patient, stimulation of the right face-selective fusiform pair elicited reported face distortions on seven real-face trials; four sham and three nearby control-pair face trials did not.
source_locators: Methods: subject and EBS; Results: EBS and distortion
alternative_explanations: Demand or reporting effects remain possible; the sham and control contrasts support causal involvement.
limitations: Repeated trials in one person, not independent people. Randomization and blinded assessor masking were not established.

claims.statement: Fusiform stimulation does not establish a unitary face center: nonspecific nonface changes occurred, naming tests were small and procedurally different, current can affect connected sites, and the two stimulated regions were not separated.
source_locators: Methods: famous face/place naming; Discussion paragraphs 2–4
alternative_explanations: A distributed circuit containing these sites is compatible with the effect.
limitations: Famous-face naming errors: 1/5 real, 2/5 sham; places: 2/5 real, 0/5 sham. Null naming differences are not equivalence. No seizure or after-discharge was reported during stimulation.

claims.statement: Scheinin et al. recruited 40 healthy young men; 39 underwent randomized open propofol (19) or dexmedetomidine (20) anesthesia and 37 returned for sleep after two withdrawals. These are overlapping arms, not 76 participants.
source_locators: Methods: Subjects and Experimental designs; Results: Physiologic sleep
alternative_explanations: Within-person control strengthens comparability without creating independent replications.
limitations: One propofol participant withdrew after randomization. Sleep occurred on average 18 weeks later; eligibility was restricted to healthy right-handed men aged 20–30.

claims.statement: Among interviewable states, Scheinin et al. reported subjective experience in 80% of anesthesia interviews and 71% of sleep interviews, including contentless impressions; these are interview rates, not population prevalence.
source_locators: Results: Realization of experimental designs; Assessment of the state of consciousness
alternative_explanations: Dreaming and memory incorporation, with report and memory selection, can produce these reports.
limitations: Exact interview numerators and denominators for these percentages are not supplied in the inspected main text. Later prose shifts the 80% figure to arousable subjects; this remains a unit inconsistency. No extrapolation to deep unarousable anesthesia.

claims.statement: State-linked relative PET blood-flow changes involved thalamic, cingulate and angular regions; fixed infusion and within-subject awakenings improved the comparisons, but these remain neural associations within manipulated states, not focal necessity or sufficiency tests.
source_locators: Methods: Neuroimaging analysis; Figure 3; Discussion
alternative_explanations: Arousal, attention, motor access, reporting and memory can contribute.
limitations: Disconnection contrasts: propofol 19, dexmedetomidine 14, sleep 9; reconnection: propofol 9, dexmedetomidine 16. Propofol loss used moderate sedation versus UR with different doses because only two reached UR2. PET integrates over 90 seconds.

claims.statement: The anesthesia study notes that absent response or recalled content cannot conclusively establish absent experience or environmental awareness; three awareness-report states were excluded from its disconnected contrasts.
source_locators: Assessment of the state of consciousness; Results: realization; Discussion limitations
alternative_explanations: Memory failure, stimulus salience and output impairment can hide experience.
limitations: One propofol and one dexmedetomidine awareness report followed UR2, and one followed N2 sleep; these need not be three disjoint people across overlapping arms. The initial anesthesia dream question preceded PET, while the detailed interview followed PET.

claims.statement: Tasserie et al. studied five male rhesus macaques: two DBS animals and three awake comparators, with previously published awake auditory data reused. The intervention unit is two animals.
source_locators: Methods: Animals and Event-related auditory task
alternative_explanations: Comparisons cannot remove all differences between DBS animals and separate awake animals.
limitations: Do not pool animals, sessions, voxels or reused datasets. Detailed session counts and exclusions in uninspected supplements remain gaps.

claims.statement: Under maintained propofol, high central-thalamic stimulation increased the reported arousal score from 0/11 to 9/11 in both DBS macaques; low CT reached 3/11 and ventrolateral stimulation remained 0/11. This supports causal modulation of behavioral arousal under these conditions.
source_locators: Results: Behavioral effects; Figure 2E; Methods: stimulation protocol
alternative_explanations: Stimulation can recruit widespread axons and arousal pathways rather than only local cell bodies.
limitations: Awake score 11/11; stimulation was 3 V versus 5 V at 130.208 Hz. Behavior was assessed outside the scanner without paralysis. Blinding and randomized condition order were not established in the inspected text.

claims.statement: High CT stimulation also shifted fMRI dynamics and enhanced hierarchical auditory responses, but subjective awareness was inferred from signatures; no auditory VL-control data were acquired and anesthetic fMRI used paralysis.
source_locators: Figure 6; Methods: anesthesia and auditory task; Discussion
alternative_explanations: Arousal, sensory gating or processing may restore markers without proving a specific subjective content.
limitations: Separate awake animals and reused data; passive local-global task, without trialwise experience reports. Medial nuclei and axonal spread, plus physiological changes, limit localization. This is not proof of efficacy in human brain injury.

claims.statement: Cogitate recruited 256 across fMRI (120), MEG (102) and iEEG (34), retaining 108, 97 and 32 respectively. Main noninvasive tests used 73 fMRI and 65 MEG held-out datasets; invasive data were not split.
source_locators: Methods: Participants; Supplement section 14
alternative_explanations: Analysis-specific samples and clinical coverage constrain modality comparisons.
limitations: fMRI exclusions: eight motion, two coverage, two incomplete; MEG: two behavior, two noise, one reconstruction; iEEG: two incomplete. Three iEEG patients below the behavior threshold were retained as a declared deviation. iEEG analyses used 31 for activation, 29 for decoding and 28 for RSA.

claims.statement: Cogitate tested suprathreshold visual category, identity, orientation and duration while varying task relevance; it did not directly contrast conscious with unconscious processing or perturb candidate brain regions.
source_locators: Figure 1; Methods: Procedure; Supplement section 3
alternative_explanations: Visible-stimulus responses may include unconscious processing; task irrelevance does not guarantee absence of attention.
limitations: Durations were 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 seconds across four categories. A separate 39-person surprise-memory control supports encoding of irrelevant items but cannot certify continuous awareness of every feature or offset on each main-study trial.

claims.statement: Operational predictions contrasted posterior versus prefrontal decoding, posterior duration tracking versus prefrontal onset/offset ignition, and posterior versus long-range prefrontal synchrony; core mathematical theories were not directly computed or exhaustively tested.
source_locators: Preregistered predictions; Protocol Experiment 1; biological focus
alternative_explanations: Auxiliary biological implementations and measurement assumptions can be revised.
limitations: Prediction centrality differed: IIT decoding was noncritical. The published 2023 protocol is an earlier version, not a complete audit of OSF timestamps.

claims.statement: Results partly supported sustained posterior representations and transient prefrontal category decoding, but the expected prefrontal offset profile and sustained posterior gamma synchrony were not established; no overall theory winner follows.
source_locators: Results predictions 1–3; Extended Data Figure 7
alternative_explanations: Coverage, macroscopic mixed selectivity, awareness timing and sampling could affect null results.
limitations: PFC orientation decoding appeared only in MEG with leakage uncertainty; identity was absent in PFC and posterior face orientation was not sustained. The outcome is mixed, not total refutation of either theory.

claims.statement: Preregistered pairwise phase consistency supported neither critical connectivity prediction; additional exploratory dynamic functional connectivity partly supported GNWT and still lacked sustained posterior connectivity.
source_locators: Results: Interareal connectivity; Supplement section 14, items 5–8
alternative_explanations: PPC noise and sparse V1/V2 sampling can reduce sensitivity; DFC measures amplitude co-modulation rather than phase.
limitations: Do not relabel DFC as preregistered confirmation. Main fMRI connectivity pooled task conditions. The cited coverage comparison has 12 V1/V2 electrodes versus 472 in PFC, and relevant posterior pair analyses involved only four patients.

claims.statement: The 2023 protocol made offset ignition conditional on conscious detection in its GNW overview and described it as possible in analysis 2; elsewhere it described onset/offset as the tested expectation. This qualifies claims that the later offset objection was entirely post hoc.
source_locators: Protocol GNW overview and Experiment 1 analysis 2; Nature prediction 2
alternative_explanations: Failure of a committed operational test can still challenge the model even when it is not an unconditional whole-theory prediction.
limitations: Original and amended OSF files were not audited; retain the wording tension rather than select a convenient version.

claims.statement: Naccache and colleagues argue that assumptions about offset attention, continuous awareness and macroscopic PFC decoding limit the Nature challenge; they also deny that activity-silent storage is mandatory for GNWT.
source_locators: Critique: offset, decoding and duration sections; Supplement section 13, pp.122–124
alternative_explanations: The consortium argues in the original discussion that strong suprathreshold signals, multimodal controls and prior agreements make failures informative.
limitations: This is a documented argument, not measured inattention. The critique says category and orientation decoding were lacking, although Nature found category decoding; do not adopt that wording as an empirical result. Its name correction does not repair this wording.

claims.statement: IIT proponents accept the failed sustained gamma-synchrony prediction but propose coverage, frequency choice and relaxed ROI criteria as limitations; their posterior-sufficiency interpretation is an argument, not a direct inactivation result.
source_locators: Supplement sections 12–12.1, pp.119–122; Nature Discussion
alternative_explanations: The consortium treats missing connectivity as a substantive challenge; a different frequency cannot count as success of the original gamma prediction.
limitations: No Phi or full cause-effect structure was computed. Posterior localization fits multiple theories; ROI relaxation is acknowledged in supplementary section 14.

claims.statement: The published protocol, final article and supplement disclose analysis changes, including an original half-split versus final one-third optimization split, retained low-performance patients, altered RSA and exploratory DFC; this packet does not claim a verified OSF history.
source_locators: Protocol project status; Nature Participants; Supplement section 14, pp.124–126
alternative_explanations: Transparent deviations can be pragmatically justified while changing confirmatory weight.
limitations: Detailed supplementary analyses were not recomputed, and separate registration files remain uninspected.

claims.statement: Neural perturbations provide causal evidence for contributions to human perceptual reports and macaque arousal/access markers, while PET and theory-test recordings locate associations; they do not establish one universally necessary and sufficient neural mechanism.
source_locators: T09 cross-study inference from CL-T09-001–018
alternative_explanations: Models limited to reporting or output remain logically possible but must explain reversible, site-specific reported phenomenological effects.
limitations: Distinct studies, methods and species are not pooled; generalization requires separate validation.

claims.statement: This packet does not establish physicalist identity, fundamentality, universal consciousness, brain-independent survival, timelessness, cosmic purpose, goodness or moral authority; those conclusions need additional discriminating and bridge premises.
source_locators: T09 arguments A-T09-001–002; T01 definitions
alternative_explanations: Identity, psychophysical-law, dualist/interface and idealist accounts can accommodate causal neural dependence when explicitly specified.
limitations: Compatibility is not positive evidence or equal likelihood. No posterior is assigned. H-B does not mean that the brain has no influence.

arguments.name: Causal neural contributions constrain embodied mind models
premises: Site-dependent neural intervention changes reported face appearance or arousal/access markers.
Within-subject/sham/control contrasts make mere passive correlation an incomplete description.
bridge_principles: The intervention meaningfully affects the neural system relevant to the observed report/behavior.
Reports are defeasible evidence of experience; animal markers require additional validation.
arguments.conclusion: Neural processes causally contribute to embodied perception and state functions in these tested contexts; models denying any such contribution are challenged.
arguments.strongest_objection: Interventions may alter access/reporting, distributed routing or a posited interface without proving how experience is constituted.
arguments.strongest_reply: An interface account must specify predictions for the observed content, site and state effects rather than merely accommodate them.

arguments.name: Neural dependence does not by itself settle ontology
premises: Causal modulation does not establish metaphysical identity.
Unresponsiveness and absent markers do not directly verify phenomenal absence.
Theory tests depend on biological and measurement assumptions.
bridge_principles: A metaphysical conclusion needs a discriminating prediction or an independently justified bridge.
arguments.conclusion: Results constrain embodied models without uniquely selecting physicalism or brain independence, or licensing survival claims from failures of a neural theory.
arguments.strongest_objection: An unspecified interface view can fit any data and lose predictive force against explicit neural mechanisms.
arguments.strongest_reply: Require prospective contrasting predictions; logical underdetermination does not make alternatives equally supported.
